name: Jacinda Ardern
role: Prime Minister of New Zealand (2017–2023), Labour leader
summary: Centre-left Labour politician who led a Labour-led government focused on climate action, child poverty and wellbeing policy, Treaty partnership with Māori, and multilateralism. Her government enacted a semi-automatic firearms ban, abortion decriminalisation, a conversion practices ban and a 39 percent top tax rate, while ruling out a capital gains tax.

limit-guns.rationale: Her government banned military-style semi-automatic firearms, assault rifles and high-capacity magazines within weeks of the Christchurch attack, with an amnesty and buy-back.

abortion-legal.rationale: Her government's Abortion Legislation Act 2020 removed abortion from the criminal law and allows it on request in early pregnancy.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Her government wrote the 1.5C and 2050 net-zero targets into law with emissions budgets and a Climate Change Commission.

human-caused-global-warming.rationale: In UN speeches she says Pacific states have contributed least to global climate change and calls for emissions cuts, treating warming as caused by human emissions.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Her government legislated child poverty reduction targets and reporting duties, a role for the state well beyond protecting against violence.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The Child Poverty Reduction Act makes reducing poverty a statutory government duty with targets and annual reporting.

unions-good.rationale: Her government's 2018 amendments gave unions workplace access and union delegates paid time, and strengthened bargaining rules.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Employment Relations Amendment Act 2018 strengthened collective bargaining rules, including duties to conclude agreements.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Her government's Fair Pay Agreements Act set up sector-wide bargaining, with unions and employers negotiating minimum terms recognised by law.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Her government added a 39 percent bracket on income over $180,000, but ruled out a capital gains tax while she led.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Her government added a higher income tax bracket of 39 percent on income over $180,000, a graduated rate structure rather than a single rate.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: Her government raised income tax on top earners by adding a 39 percent bracket, the opposite of abolishing the tax.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Her government ended new offshore petroleum exploration permits, while existing permits and onshore Taranaki exploration continued.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The 2021 Births, Deaths, Marriages and Relationships Registration Act, passed under her government, created a self-identification process for registered sex.

assisted-dying.rationale: She disclosed that she voted yes in the 2020 End of Life Choice referendum.

armed-resistance-to-occupation.rationale: Her government gave Ukraine military assistance, including body armour, equipment and later training, to help it resist Russia's invasion.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: After the Supreme Court's 2022 ruling she said she personally supports lowering the voting age, and her government moved to draft a bill.

apologise-for-past-wrongs.rationale: She delivered a formal, unreserved government apology for the Dawn Raids of the 1970s.

nation-first.rationale: In UN speeches she says going it alone is not an option for New Zealand and defends multilateralism and collective action.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: She says nuclear weapons do not make anyone safer and calls on states to join the treaty prohibiting them, citing New Zealand's nuclear-free stand.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: She says New Zealand has never accepted mutually assured destruction and would choose disarmament over deterrence by nuclear weapons.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: She says nuclear weapons do not make states safer and that New Zealand rejects the logic of nuclear deterrence.

recognize-territorial-claims-from-conque.rationale: She calls Russia's invasion of Ukraine illegal and a direct attack on the UN Charter and the rules-based order.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: She lists the introduction of same-sex marriage among the achievements in the laws New Zealand passed.

proportional-representation.rationale: She describes New Zealand's MMP system, in which every vote counts and Parliament better reflects communities, as a strength.

democracy-best.rationale: In her Harvard address she describes democracy as an imperfect but precious system giving equal voice to the weak and the strong, and urges defending it.

one-party-rule.rationale: She defends democracy as giving equal voice to all and warns against controlling debate, which contradicts exclusive party rule.

future-generations.rationale: In her valedictory she says climate action is owed to the next generation.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In her Waitangi speech she says the Treaty partnership is not yet passing the test on Māori health and defends the Māori Health Authority as a remedy.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: She calls for living free from racism and discrimination on religion, gender, sexuality or ethnicity for everyone, and for human rights norms.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: She condemns discrimination on ethnicity and says safety requires freedom from racism for everyone.

political-violence-legitimate.rationale: She calls the Christchurch attack the work of a terrorist and led the Christchurch Call against terrorist content online.

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: Her government made climate-related disclosure mandatory for large listed companies, insurers, banks and managers, a legal duty to report climate impacts.

notes: Researched: UN speeches 2018-2022, Harvard 2022, valedictory 2023, enacted legislation 2018-2022, tax, wages, Covid mandates, referendums. Many statements have no stated position and stay null.
